newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker, hit new lows near close.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker, hit new lows near close.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled weaker and barely off the new life-of-contract lows hit just ahead of the close, but volume remained thin, dealers said.
They blamed losses on speculative selling which set off sell stops below 73.50 cents in September. The contract fell to a lifetime low of 73.35 cents where light trade buying supported the market.
The benchmark September contract closed 0.40 cent lower at 73.45 cents a lb, having ranged from 74.30 to a new contract low of 73.35 cents. The rest of the board finished down 0.15 to 0.85 cent.
Analysts said a bearish technical and fundamental outlook will continue to pressure prices and pegged nearby support at 72.00 cents followed by 70.00 cents in September.

A record Florida crop of 225.7 million 90-lb boxes is estimated for this year with an even larger crop forecast for 1997/98, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said. Brazil is also expected to produce a record crop of 18.3 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Meanwhile, retail sales remain slack and prices high, a combination that suggests ending stocks will continue to build.

"This should keep downward pressure on the market," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said in a weekly citrus comment. "We would not be surprised to see the lows of around 65.00 cents penetrated if the October USDA crop report is much above 230-235 million boxes."
A technical analyst said the Elliot Wave showed the market was in a fifth wave down with resistance seen at 67.80 cents.
An estimated 1,500 lots changed hands on the day compared with Thursday's official 1,664 lots.
